title: Every protocol has at least one leaf
statement: Let $p$ be a deterministic two-party communication protocol over input types $X$ (Alice) and $Y$ (Bob) with output type $\alpha$. Then the number of leaves of $p$ — that is, the number of output nodes in its tree shape — is strictly positive, and so is at least one.
hypotheses_covered: p is a deterministic communication protocol over input types X, Y with output type α
replaced:
For every deterministic protocol $p : \mathrm{Protocol}\;X\;Y\;\alpha$, the number of
leaves satisfies $0 < \texttt{CommunicationComplexity.Deterministic.Protocol.numLeaves}\;p$.
In particular, the leaf count of a protocol is always at least one.
